attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No valid derivation converts an arbitrary small H_N circuit into a charged sparse quotient-polynomial sketch. Without this extraction, sketch lower bounds are falsifier tests, not source lower bounds.
steps: Start from the quotient normal form H_N=<a_N,I_N(x)> over F_2 for the XOR carrier.
Observe that cycle 57's low-degree feature bound gives C(H_N)<=S_T+binom(r,<=t)+E_N N when the final combiner has degree t.
Test the converse direction: high degree does not imply high circuit cost, because a degree-r monomial needs only O(r) gates after feature computation.
Replace the degree parameter by monomial support A_N and derive C(H_N)<=S_T+O(A_N r_N+E_N N).
Check target preservation separately: SAT in SIZE(n^c) still gives C(H_N)<=N^{max{rho,q}+o(1)} for polylogarithmic queries.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Hardness-magnification bridge via XOR carriers and sparse quotient-polynomial falsifiers

assumptions: Source lower-bound model is general nonuniform Boolean circuit size C(H_N), with the desired threshold C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.
Generator cost is C(G_N)<=N^{rho+o(1)} and all generated formulas have length L_N=(log N)^d.
The sparse sketch has P_N(z)=xor_{A in M_N^*} prod_{i in A} z_i over F_2 with support size A_N=|M_N^*|.
The sketch may be wrong on at most E_N inputs, and those exceptions are patched by equality circuits at cost O(E_N N).
definitions: source object: H_N:{0,1}^N -> {0,1}, H_N(x)=xor_{j<=M_N} SAT(F_{N,j}(x)), with M_N=N^q and formula length L_N=(log N)^d.
target object: nonuniform Boolean circuits for SAT_n; the target consequence is SAT notin SIZE(n^c) for every fixed c, hence NP not subset P/poly under the usual encoding.
controlled interface: substitute an assumed SAT circuit of size L_N^c into every generated query and charge the generator, query fanout, and final XOR explicitly.
target-preserving condition: L_N=(log N)^d, d>1, max{rho,q}<1+epsilon, no target advice is hidden in the generator beyond the fixed nonuniform carrier family.

SAT-preserving quotient: a partition U_N of generated formulas into blocks with a well-defined SAT label a_u, while I_{N,u}(x) records the parity of positions whose generated formula falls in block u.

charged quotient feature: T_N:{0,1}^N -> {0,1}^{r_N} has total circuit cost S_T and is charged separately from the final polynomial; allowing an uncharged H_N feature would make the audit tautological.

equations.label: quotient-inner-product-normal-form
equations.latex: H_N(x)=\bigoplus_{u\in U_N} a_u I_{N,u}(x)=\langle a_N,I_N(x)\rangle_{\mathbb F_2}.
equations.valid_when: Valid when U_N is a SAT-preserving quotient of the generated formulas and I_N records parity incidence per quotient class.

equations.label: target-substitution-upper-bound
equations.valid_when: Applies when SAT on length L_N formulas has nonuniform size L_N^c and the generator is target-clean.

equations.label: sparse-sketch-upper-bound
equations.latex: H_N=P_N(T_N)\text{ off }B_N,\ |B_N|=E_N\ \Rightarrow\ C(H_N)\le S_T+O(A_N r_N+E_N N).
equations.valid_when: Requires that all feature circuits are charged once, monomial gates share them, and exceptions are patched by equality tests.

equations.label: exponent-falsifier-threshold
equations.latex: S_T\le N^\sigma,\ A_N\le N^\alpha,\ r_N\le N^\gamma,\ E_N\le N^\eta\ \Rightarrow\ C(H_N)\le N^{\max\{\sigma,\alpha+\gamma,1+\eta\}+o(1)}.
equations.valid_when: Valid when the parameter exponents are asymptotic and r_N is at most N^{gamma+o(1)}.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If max{sigma,alpha+gamma,1+eta}<1+epsilon, the proposed H_N lower bound is false; if features are uncharged or allowed to be the H_N circuit itself, the gate is not a valid route-specific audit.

assumptions: The feature map T_N is already charged by S_T.
The final combiner is implemented as a fan-in-two Boolean circuit with shared feature outputs.

definitions: degree audit: ruling out P(T) only for deg(P)<=t.
support audit: ruling out P(T) with small number of monomials, regardless of maximum monomial degree.
high-degree sparse combiner: P(z)=prod_{i<=r} z_i has degree r but support one.

equations.label: single-high-degree-monomial-cost
equations.valid_when: Valid when the feature outputs are shared and the monomial is implemented by a balanced AND tree.

equations.label: low-degree-support-relation

candidate_lemmas.statement: A low-degree quotient-feature lower-bound audit is incomplete. The correct necessary audit must rule out sparse polynomial support independently of degree, since a single monomial of degree r_N costs only O(r_N) gates after the features are computed.

assumptions: The carrier remains an explicit real-SAT carrier, not an oracle-defined planted-control carrier.

definitions: extraction theorem needed: every circuit of size N^{1+epsilon-delta} for H_N yields T_N,P_N,B_N with S_T+A_N r_N+E_N N <= N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.
barrier status: the desired extraction is nonrelativizing and SAT-specific; sparse-sketch absence alone is outside a valid lower-bound proof.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 58 repairs the XOR-carrier audit: low degree was the wrong nonlinear measure. The valid upper-bound falsifier is sparse quotient-polynomial support with threshold S_T+A_N r_N+E_N N<N^{1+epsilon}. This preserves the polylog-query target bridge but narrows the source obligation and exposes a new extraction gap: sparse-sketch hardness is not yet general-circuit hardness.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No fixed b,a tradeoff rules out all polynomial-time exponents. Space-capped tradeoffs do not quantify over all P algorithms. Padding can preserve NP-hardness while collapsing the measured exponent.
steps: Assume a uniform theorem: every deterministic decider A for SAT_m in model M has T_A(m)S_A(m)^a >= m^b.
Assume toward a fixed-exponent transfer that SAT has an algorithm A with T_A(m)<=m^k.
Use the controlled interface S_A(m)<=T_A(m)polylog(m), giving T_A(m)^{a+1}polylog(m)^a >= m^b.
Conclude T_A(m)>=m^{b/(a+1)}/polylog(m), so the assumed m^k algorithm is contradicted only if b/(a+1)>k.
For a theorem restricted to S<=m^s, first verify S_A(m)<=m^s; time m^k alone supplies no such verification when k>s.
Under padding M=n^c, rewrite any core exponent b in the full target length as b/c, so padding can erase the margin against any fixed k.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation proves only a conditional fixed-k lower bound. P != NP would need a family of valid SAT tradeoffs with b>(a+1)k for every k, or a stronger time-only lower bound; neither is supplied.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: time-space tradeoff exponent gate

assumptions: The machine model is fixed before comparing source and target, e.g. multitape Turing machine or log-cost RAM with standard space accounting.
The tradeoff lower bound quantifies over deterministic deciders for the same SAT encoding, not over a promise slice with hidden decompression.
The alleged P algorithm is uniform; nonuniform circuit consequences require a separate simulation and are not inferred here.
Polylogarithmic overhead in the space<=time simulation is negligible only after an explicit exponent margin b>(a+1)k.
definitions: source object: a uniform time-space tradeoff lower bound for SAT_m in a named machine model M, stated as T(m)S(m)^a >= m^b or under S(m)<=m^s.
target object: deterministic polynomial-time decision of SAT on m-bit encodings, audited exponent-by-exponent as DTIME(m^k).
controlled interface: the only transfer uses the universal inequality S_A(m)<=O(T_A(m) polylog m) for standard uniform machines; no circuit, advice, or proof-system inference is smuggled in.

target-preserving condition: the lower bound must be on the same SAT encoding length m and must cover the space used by the alleged m^k-time algorithm; padding changes the exponent and must be explicitly accounted for.

equations.label: source_tradeoff
equations.valid_when: Valid when the source lower-bound model quantifies over all deterministic deciders in the named machine model on the same SAT_m slice.

equations.label: space_time_interface
equations.valid_when: Applies for standard Turing or RAM models where all written cells are reached during the counted computation.

equations.label: time_exponent_transfer
equations.valid_when: Requires the tradeoff lower bound to cover the actual space of A and uses only S_A<=T_A polylog m.

equations.label: dt_k_exclusion_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when k is fixed before the transfer and constants in the polylog overhead are dominated by the exponent margin.

equations.label: restricted_space_domain
equations.latex: A\in DTIME(m^k)\text{ is covered by }S\le m^s\text{ only when }S_A(m)\le m^s
equations.valid_when: Applies when the source theorem is conditional on an a priori space cap rather than all polynomial spaces.

equations.label: padding_erosion
equations.valid_when: Applies after the reduction pads an n-bit SAT instance to length M=n^c while preserving NP-hardness for fixed c.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Choose k>b/(a+1), or pad SAT from length n to M=n^c with c large. If the claimed P != NP consequence remains unchanged, the route ignored a valid exponent-erosion falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-level bridge and quarantine: it extracts the exact quantitative condition under which a time-space theorem can refute a fixed DTIME exponent, and blocks the invalid leap from fixed tradeoffs to P != NP.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A SAT time-space product lower bound transfers to a deterministic time lower bound only after exponent division by the space exponent. If every decider for SAT_m satisfies T(m)S(m)^a >= m^b in a named uniform model, then SAT_m is not in DTIME(m^k) only when b>(a+1)k up to polylog slack. If the lower bound is stated only for S<=m^s, it covers only alleged algorithms whose actual space lies below that cap. Thus fixed-exponent time-space tradeoffs are valid restricted-algorithm lower bounds but are not P != NP progress without an unbounded exponent family or an all-polynomial-space transfer certificate.

control_decision.pivot_test: If the next route cannot state a source exponent b, space exponent a, target k, and full-length encoding, backtrack or quarantine it.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if a theorem supplies b>(a+1)k for a named k on unpadded SAT, or an infinite family beating every k with all-polynomial-space coverage.
control_decision.reason: The branch produced a named source model, target exponent, controlled interface, and padding falsifier. It certifies when a time-space theorem is useful and when the P != NP extrapolation is invalid.

dependency_updates.description: Any time-space lower-bound route must record the product exponent a, source exponent b, target time exponent k, and whether the theorem covers all spaces or only S<=m^s.
NP-hardness-preserving padding is now an explicit falsifier for source measures stated on a decompressed core rather than the full target length.
Time-space diagonalization and simulation arguments are mostly relativizing; a claimed main-theorem transfer must identify a nonrelativizing feature rather than rely on the product gate alone.

Uniform time-space lower bounds are not automatically natural properties against circuits; naturalness appears only after conversion to dense truth-table distinguishers, which is not used in this bridge.

falsifiers: A claimed TS^a>=m^b to P != NP bridge fails under the falsifier k>b/(a+1): an m^k-time SAT algorithm could satisfy the tradeoff rather than contradict it.
A space-capped theorem with S<=m^s is not target-preserving for P: a hypothetical m^{s+1}-time polynomial-space decider lies outside the theorem's quantified domain.
Padded SAT_c with M=n^c is a target-preserving falsifier for exponent claims measured on the core length n; NP-hardness remains for fixed c but the lower-bound exponent becomes b/c in M.

A purely relativizing diagonalization-style proof object remains barrier-suspect unless it names a nonrelativizing ingredient; the present gate is valid only as exponent accounting, not as a barrier escape.

This is route-level progress and a falsifier for fixed-exponent tradeoff slogans, not evidence for P != NP.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No generated, sparse, advice-free, globally sound, non-natural anti-ball proof family is known. The bridge is valid only after constructing such a binding certificate without a large locatable projection and without subthreshold row access.
steps: Model the source as a deterministic generator G(1^m) emitting M_m<=2^{D m+O(1)} row/proof pairs, rather than as an existential proof search problem.
Define the target language by multiplexing only the emitted rows; proofs are used for soundness but are not part of the target truth table.
If F_m has circuits of size 2^{q n_m}, fixing the emitted hard row index gives a circuit for that row of size 2^{q(1+D)m+o(m)}.
Global verifier soundness for an accepted generated pair contradicts this when q<theta/(1+D), and kappa-dense padding gives delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)).
Audit the proof relation: a poly(N) locator on a large accepted projection triggers the natural-proofs barrier, while a subthreshold indexed row decoder directly falsifies MCSP soundness.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is route-level progress: it proves a conditional transfer and names falsifiers, but it does not construct the source object or prove P != NP.

assumptions: Constants theta>0, D>=0, kappa>=1, and lambda<infty are independent of m.
The generator can be simulated deterministically in 2^{O(m)} time per requested multiplexed bit by sequential scanning; no nonuniform row index or proof advice is used.
For kappa-dense m, some emitted pair (T_{m,i},pi_{m,i}) is accepted by V_m.
Verifier soundness is for unrestricted circuits of size below 2^{theta m}; restricted or uniform lower bounds are not enough.
definitions: source object: a length-indexed deterministic generator G which sequentially emits a sparse list of truth tables and nonblackbox anti-ball proofs for MCSP no-side claims.
target object: the multiplexed E language L_G whose length n_m block has truth table F_m(i,x)=T_{m,i}(x).
controlled interface: image entropy D, hard threshold theta, length-gap kappa, generator overhead lambda, and verifier soundness against unrestricted circuits.
target-preserving condition: generation is uniform and advice-free, source lengths are kappa-dense, and the consequence is an E circuit lower bound rather than P != NP itself.
row length N=2^m; image count M_m<=2^{D m+O(1)}; multiplexed input length n_m=m+ceil(log M_m).
Global soundness means every accepted pair is hard, not merely that the generated transcript is intended to describe a hard row.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Falsifier: if the proof is only existential, uses advice to find the row/proof pair, proves hardness only for a promised transcript, or supplies an indexed decoder of size below 2^{theta m}, the bridge is not valid.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Conditional bridge theorem repairing cycle 57: proof location is handled by generation, while the quantitative extraction depends on hard-row threshold and image entropy only.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Generated anti-ball proofs give a valid MCSP-carrier bridge: let theta>0. If on kappa-dense source lengths m a deterministic no-advice generator emits at most 2^{D m+O(1)} rows T_{m,i} in {0,1}^{2^m} and proofs pi_{m,i}, at least one emitted pair is accepted, and a globally sound verifier satisfies V_m(T,pi)=1 => C(T)>2^{theta m} against unrestricted Boolean circuits, then the multiplexed language is in E and has circuit complexity 2^{delta n} for every delta<theta/(kappa(1+D)). Proof length 2^{lambda m} with constant lambda affects only the E running-time constant, not the lower-bound exponent.

assumptions: Loc is deterministic or P/poly-uniform over truth tables and runs in time poly(N).
The accepted projection has density at least N^{-c} among all truth tables.
Verifier soundness is useful against unrestricted circuits of size N^{epsilon}.
definitions: N=2^m is the truth-table length.
The accepted projection is S_m={T: exists pi with V_m(T,pi)=1}.
A locator is stronger than a generator: it maps an arbitrary row T to a proof, while the bridge only needs length-indexed generated pairs.

equations.label: large_projection
equations.valid_when: Valid when accepted rows form a large property in the Razborov-Rudich density sense.

equations.label: usefulness

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Falsifier: a repair that makes proofs easy to locate for many rows is not a sparse carrier repair; it is a natural useful property.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier audit: separates harmless generated proofs from locatable large properties that collide with the natural-proofs barrier.
candidate_lemmas.statement: A generated proof relation becomes a natural-proof-style obstruction if it also has a constructive row-to-proof locator on a large projection. If Loc runs in poly(N), V(T,Loc(T)) decides a property holding on at least N^{-c} of all N-bit truth tables, and V soundly excludes all circuits of size N^{epsilon}, then the route has built a constructive large useful property; under standard PRF assumptions this is a natural-proofs falsifier, and unconditionally it marks the object as natural rather than the required sparse non-natural carrier.

assumptions: The indexed decoder is correct for all x in {0,1}^m and for the accepted row index i.
The decoder size exponent alpha is strictly below the claimed MCSP hardness exponent theta.
definitions: The decoder input i has Dm+O(1) bits and x has m bits.
Hardwiring i is allowed because MCSP uses unrestricted nonuniform circuits for a fixed truth table.
This leakage is independent of proof length; it is an access-profile obstruction.

equations.valid_when: Applies when the row index is hardwired and the decoder computes every truth-table bit correctly.

If a circuit A_m(i,x) of size 2^{alpha m+o(m)} outputs T_{m,i}(x) for every emitted row and alpha<theta, then each emitted row has circuit complexity below 2^{theta m} after hardwiring i, contradicting any accepted theta-hard row.
